title: Nim heaps in the Game of Cycles: the parity conjecture fails on trees
summary: The Game of Cycles, invented by Francis Su, is a two-player game in which the players take turns drawing arrows on the edges of a plane graph, never creating a sink or a source. On a tree only the sink-source rule matters, and the player who makes the last move wins. Several authors conjectured that on a tree the second player wins exactly when the number of markable edges is even. We show that this parity conjecture is false, and we explain why.
